content:
ana: quick heads-up: prototyping a tolerant 'batch-fuse' layer to handle long-tail bursts in continuous-batching. goal: avoid wholesale scheduler reshuffles when a few heavy requests appear.
mike: is this another admission tweak or an independent reconciliation pass?
ana: independent reconciliation. it watches per-epoch batch fill patterns and will try to fuse underfilled microbatches into a nearby cohort without touching guaranteed allocations. think of it as a cooperative post-assembly compaction.
hannah: what about seqid/prefix guarantees and KV cache locality? fusing could reorder things.
ana: rules: 1) only fuse requests that are marked reorder_tolerant or have no kvcache_affinity tag; 2) preserve intra-request sequence by only fusing whole-request groups, never splitting a request.
ryan: how does it interact with the lease/slot lifecycle? we can't steal active leases.
mike: fuse will only operate on pending microbatches that haven't been leased yet. it will announce intent via the queue-manager API and perform a safe swap: take ownership of batch A and B as a single fused batch at the next epoch boundary.
hannah: telemetry and safety hooks?
ana: exporting: fuse_attempts_total, fuse_success_total, fuse_fail_reason{kv_affinity,lease_race,capacity}, fused_batch_p50/p95. also tag fused requests with X-Fused:batch.v1 for trace filtering. rollout shadow->small canary. auto-disable if fused_fail_rate > 5% or cluster_p99 increases >8% for 5m.
ryan: config snippet idea:

```
batch_fuse {
  enabled: true
  epoch_ms: 250
  max_fuses_per_epoch: 6
  probe_fraction: 0.02
  tag_fused_requests: "batch_fuse.v1"
}
```

mike: cost tradeoff note: fusing improves packing (fewer kernel launches) but may increase thundering risk when fused batches all hit heavy-model paths. need backoff heuristics.
ana: agreed. fuse will sample prewarm hints and will back off if prewarm_failures exceed threshold. also we provide a conservative_mode where only small requests (<128 tokens) are eligible.
hannah: adapters expecting static slab ids: will they see any changes?
ana: we preserve a stable_slab header and add fused_from metadata when we move requests. adapters can opt-out with allow_fuse=false per-route. default keeps compatibility.
ryan: any simulation results?
ana: initial sims on mixed traces: p50 raw latency down ~10-18% under bursty injections, cost per-token down ~4%. tail unaffected in baseline sims; will run more canary workloads.
mike: please add unit tests for lease races and a small chaos job to simulate delayed prewarm.
ana: on it. PR will include perf harness and dashboard panels. PR link (draft): github.com/redwood/retenge/pull/1407
deploy-bot: release 'batch-fuse/v0.1' created by @ana. CI green.
hannah: i'll own observability. add filters for fused vs unfused p99.
ana: rollout plan: shadow 48h, then 5% -> 25% -> 100% with kill-switch batch_fuse.enabled=false. will add FAQ on when to opt-out and expected delta. thanks all.
